title: Measles antibodies (immunity check)
what: This blood test shows whether you are protected against measles.
why: If you do not remember being vaccinated, before pregnancy, for health workers and teachers, before travel, and during measles outbreaks.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 5 days
tell_doctor: If and when you had measles vaccines
If you had immunoglobulin or a blood transfusion in recent months

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast strictly, but it is better to come 3 to 4 hours after a light, non-fatty meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: After a vaccine
prepare.text: If you were recently vaccinated, you do not need the test right away. Your doctor will say when.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A sleeve you can easily roll up above the elbow.

bring: Your referral or list of tests
Your vaccination certificate, if you have it
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow, and you are asked to clench your fist a few times
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick. Blood fills the tubes in a few seconds
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
If you are not protected, the doctor may offer a vaccine
Keep the result with your vaccination records
red_flags: The puncture site is very swollen, painful, and red

faq.q: If antibodies are low, do I need another vaccine?
faq.a: Often, yes. Your doctor decides based on your vaccine history.

faq.q: Can I get the vaccine during pregnancy?
faq.a: No. The measles vaccine is not given in pregnancy. That is why it is better to check your protection before you get pregnant.

reminders.text: Measles antibody test tomorrow. Bring your vaccination certificate.
